speaker: Balthier
line_text: Balthier Planning on leaving me behind, were you?

speaker: Fermon
line_text: I was just telling these youngsters about the ruins in the Tchita Uplands. Been my life's work studying them. According to legend, an ancient people sealed away a terrible wyrm in those ruins. Four shrines there were, each with an iron colossus to hold the wyrm at bay. But now a wyrm roams the Uplands once more... These wyrms are one and the same, I'm certain. Hm? Ah, you've come about the bill. Then I ask you to kill the beast before it grows too strong. The beast is the Lindwyrm. Will you hunt it? (choices: Accept / Decline) / The iron colossuses of Tchita Uplands are only legend. No proof of them or the wyrm have I found. But with your help, find it I shall. You must fell the wyrm before it regains its lost strength. They say it will only appear under cover of cloud. Search with this in mind. If the legends are to be believed, the Lindwyrm keeps to the highlands in Tchita. I pray you find it in time... / As you like. / I was just telling these youngsters a story about the ruins in the Tchita Uplands. How many years I've spent in their study. How many more to come... / So, you have slain the mighty Lindwyrm of the Tchita Uplands! Thank you, my boy. You have rid the world of a terror from its past. / Yes? A rusted scrap of armor? What of it? Could it be...? Proof that the iron colossuses were real? What fortune!

speaker: Jules
line_text: With your help, I've made myself a pretty bit o' coin of late. Many thanks, boy. Hope to do business with you again soon. Heh heh. / Might a boy be in the market for some... information? Sorry, I've none worth selling. Such a boy would be wise to pass on anything he heard to me, though... I'll pay a good price for word of goings-on in the Ministry of Law and the Senate. A boy could stand to make a profit... / Boy. There's a man near here who goes by the name of "Beasley." Tell him what you just learned. / Boy. You've seen the moogles dancing nearby? Go and tell them what you've just learned. / Boy. There's a young man in the Alley of Low Whispers who's recently come from the City. Go and tell him what you've just learned. / A boy would do well to pass on any knowledge he came by on the streets. Depending on the flavor, I might be convinced to part with some coin...

speaker: Imperial
line_text: Entering the capital? You have credentials? (choices: I have. / I have not.) / Hm? Well I don't see any! We can't just throw open our gates to you vulgars, you know. Especially not the lying kind! Away with you! / No credentials!? We can't just throw open our gates to any old riff-raff who happen to be passing by. Be off with you, commoner! / Bah, we see naught but brawling and loutishness down here. If you start something, don't expect to be let off lightly!

speaker: Disparaging Woman
line_text: Trying to go up to Archades, perchance? I know the type. All hopes an' dreams, but never any knowledge. Ye wouldn't venture into battle without a blade, am I right? To go to the City without the proper knowledge, why, 'tis the same thing. And I'll tell ye summat else: it was knowledge what brought them Senators to their knees, an' that's the truth. Still want to go to the City? / Ye've been to the City I hear... How was it? I've a mind to go meself. Someday.

speaker: Fallen Man
line_text: Best not speak to me, lest my ill luck rub off on you. I lost everything... Everything! Ah, if I'd only had the right information... / Best not speak to me, lest my ill luck rub off on you. I lost everything... Everything! Ah, if I'd only had the right information...

speaker: Trembling Woman
line_text: People 'round 'ere? They're the ones wot didn't make it up there. Dregs. Dropouts. Ah, 'ow I tire o' the vulgar life... But I'll get out.

speaker: Frustrated Woman
line_text: I've plans to go to the City with my beau... But he's kept me waiting for hours! I expect he's lost. (sigh) He's so provincial. / I've plans to go to the City with my beau... But he's kept me waiting for hours! Mayhap I'll go on ahead by myself.

speaker: Broken Man
line_text: I spent some time in the City, once...gatherin' up all the information I could lay me 'ands on. But it turns out some of it weren't true... an' before long I ended up back down 'ere. / I was played false by false information up in the City... Then it occurred to me, I should be the one doing the playin'. That's the way to do it...

speaker: Fermon
line_text: Come to hear a tale, perhaps? There's a lot to be learned from the stories of the past...a lot you youngsters seem to have forgotten. To your peril. You should show a little more respect...for faerie tales.

speaker: Otto; Ridelle
line_text: You think you might...not stare at me? I'm in the midst of a very important conversation. / See this? 'Tis a wedding band of moonsilver! / Ridelle I... You didn't have to give me this! Why, your words alone give me joy enough... / What're you staring at? Something against cross- class relations? You think that two people from different backgrounds can't share true love? I'll have you know that when I first came down here, it was her who took me in. Without her, I'd still be in a gutter somewhere, friendless. Kindness like hers you won't find up there in the City, mark my words! There's no place for it. Can't you see? Or are you blinded by your chops? / So I said, "To the underworld with class! To the underworld with status!" And I proposed. / Her favorite story's "The Prince on the Moon," see? So I'm giving her a ring made of moonsilver! / What? You don't think that's roman— Eh? You're looking for moonsilver? A medallion? Well, why didn't you say so! I had to take a chunk off for the ring, but if this will suffice, it's yours. / I've helped you out. I've given you the medallion. Maybe you could say a little prayer for us in return. That'd be right decent of you.

speaker: Shifty-Eyed Man
line_text: Know where the Alley of Muted Sighs got 'er name? See, there's two kinds o' people 'ere: them as want to go up to the City... An' them as want to keep those people down 'ere where they belong, tellin' 'em lies, an' spreadin' misinformation to confuse 'em. Them poor ones wot never made it up...they're the ones wot are sighin', see? You...weren't 'eaded up to the City, were ya? / It's important to grab wotever information comes yer way...but just as important to know wot ya can and can't trust. Who, me? Heh heh! Oh, you can trust me, son! You can trust me...

speaker: Little Sister
line_text: 'Ello there. Mmm? Oh, don't bother tryin' to talk to 'er. Me sister's not stopped lookin' off into the distance since 'er fella went up to the City... / Me sister's had a letter from 'er fella. What's it say? She ain't even told me that... But she seems well 'appy, an' that's wot matters, innit?

speaker: Lucky Man
line_text: Psst. I'll tell ye a secret, but it stays between us two, right? I spied summat in-credible jus' now. What? Wouldn't ye like to know! 'Twas a bag o' coin! Jus' thrown in a barrel, it was. With a hoard like that, the City'll be me oyster! Now don't go tellin' anyone, ye hear? / Psst. Don't be tellin' a soul, but I found me this big sack o' coins, right? But then its owner found me, see... I've ne'er been so sore in all me life... Now don't go tellin' anyone, ye hear? / Oi! Ye couldn't keep yer gob shut, could ye? Ye went an' told someone what was meant to stay between us. A right rotten thing to do, was that.

speaker: Indefatigable Granny
line_text: Eh, me? I'm ready t' begin a new life up in the City, that's for sure. I been tricked out of all I owned before, but this time, I'll go prepared. / I was all ready t' begin a new life up in the City, but me grandson, he convinced me otherwise. I suppose I belong here...sad as that makes me.

speaker: Worried Grandson
line_text: Me gran's got me worried. She keeps on talkin' about goin' to the City, an' makin' 'er fortune. Makin' 'er fortune!? She's old! / Me gran's given up on the City for good, it seems. I just 'ope she doesn't get any other barmy ideas into 'er 'ead.

speaker: Beasley
line_text: Don't think ye can look down on me. I'm savin' me gil to get out of here and up there. Why, I've got a bag full o' coin put aside already... That is, I had a bag full o' coin, till someone come along and stole it! Grr... I was sure it'd be safe as houses in that barrel, too... / Whaaaat!? Yer tellin' me that ye know the bloke what's taken me coin!? Oh, it was him, was it? / I had all me savin's stolen, but luckily I got 'em back. I'm just preparin' meself for the journey up to the City, now. How about you? Are you prepared? Deep down? Really? Oh. All right, well, best o' luck then. / Hey, er, thanks mate. Got me bag o' coins back. I'm just preparin' meself for the journey up to the City, now. How about you? Are you prepared? Deep down? Really? Oh. All right, well, best o' luck then.

speaker: Nay-Sayer
line_text: You going on from 'ere? On from 'ere's Archades. You go there, you'd best watch yerself. People there, they'd pluck the feathers from a livin' chocobo if they thought they could make a profit on 'em. I'd turn back if I was you. / Oh, it's you... I 'eard you'd been gettin' into all sorts of places you shouldn't, up in the City. Surprised you've come back from 'em.

speaker: Nervous Seeq
line_text: The City's just up these stairs... Me head says all I've gotta do is walk up 'em, but me feet are tremblin', what with the assassination an' all. / You...you went to the City, did you? That's quite somethin', that is. I thought to go up there meself, but me feet went all of a tingle...

speaker: Loiterer
line_text: I tire of swapping tidbits of information in the street...though there's naught else I fancy doin', truth be told. That's the problem with success... / You seem to be keeping yerself busy. Busy's good. Busy's profitable. Tell me a tale of home someday, will ya? Of Rabanastre, I mean. See? There ain't much I don't know!

speaker: Indecisive Man
line_text: I've been told that joining the Watch is a good way to get on in the world...yet others tell me it's a hard life...full of hard choices. What to do...? What to be...? That's the problem with having too much information: 'tis difficult to make up your mind! / Should I go to the City? Should I not? Is there no way to get ahead, other than the soldiering life? Hmm...I hear that fellow sitting on the corner over there used to be a Judge. Mayhap he'll be able to advise me.

speaker: Ex-Broker
line_text: I played many a man false in the City, so I did. 'Course, I was bein' played just the same, though I didn't know it. I've ruined so many men... 'Tis all I can do now to hide meself here 'n' hope I don't run into any former "clients." / I've given up o' late. No good comes of tryin', so why try? I'm startin' to think the best thing to do is live 'n' die here...in peace 'n' quiet. / The thing I feared most has come to pass. One o' them that I swindled up in the City's found me! Where am I to hide now, I ask ye!?

speaker: Cockatrice
line_text: Me? I've lived here for a good while, now, but I had a jolly hard time when I first arrived. The City was a far cry from my native Giza, you see. But I've seen much in this town. People of all walks of life... Life...now there's a fascinating thing. I've seen plenty of men who've failed at it. Lost their hope and then their happiness... Most sad. Why, hope's the most important thing of all... We cockatrices, we must hold on to hope even when our days in this world seem to be numbered. Me? I hope to see my homeland once more... / (It's an old but dignified fowl.)

speaker: Man at the Gate
line_text: Hrm? Now this is new. Plenty o' worms come up out o' the ground 'ere, but not many of 'em are the sort wi' two legs. Come to make your fortune in th' capital? A word of advice, worms: turn back while ye've still some gil to yer name. / I've 'eard o' ye. Yer the lad o' seven-and-ten what's come from Rabanastre. Talk is that ye've the prodigal Bunansa in yer party, what's more.

speaker: Wary Woman
line_text: Welcome to Archades...Old Archades, that is. The people 'ere, they all took their dreams up to the City, 'ad 'em stripped away, an' fell back down. / Welcome to Archades... If you want to see yer dreams come true, be a soldier. The people down 'ere, they're the ones what refused. They wouldn't take up the sword, and look what 'appened: spent 'n' shriveled, the lot of 'em. You want somethin', you pay the price.

speaker: Stairbottom Elder
line_text: Yours is an unfamiliar face. If you're here hoping to go up to the City, best find yourself information that's like to interest the ardents and gentry. Word travels fast in this town. New information is born, grows old, and dies in a day. The Emperor's assassination? Ancient history, my friend. / And there I was thinking you'd come here without a scrap of information to your name... Imagine my surprise when I found out you'd got a lot more than a scrap...that you were very well informed indeed...

speaker: Precocious Girl
line_text: Come to buy information, or, perhaps, to sell? Knowledge is what makes this town work. Why, if I had gil or a chop to spare, I'd make an offer for what ye know right now... / Yer the prodigal Bunansa, eh? Hrm... Yer shorter than I imagined ye.

speaker: Stranded Merchant
line_text: Meh! Lost all my money... Can't even afford an airship back home to Rabanastre! Aye, I thought of going back through Sochen, but I hear some ancient wyrm lurks down there, and I don't much care to run into one of those. You think I could get away on these legs!? Bah! I'm stuck here for life. Look, wouldya buy something to help a fellow out? (snort) / I'm saving gil to get back home to Rabanastre. Buy something to help a fellow out?

speaker: Cautious Woman
line_text: Headed to the City, are ye? Going to be a soldier like the rest of 'em? I wish ye luck. Ye go up there, you die a little inside. Aye, a part of ye goes cold an' black. Just like them senators... I'd stay down here, if I were you. / Headed to the City, are ye? Going to be a soldier like the rest of 'em? I wish ye luck. Just...think on what ye'll lose 'well as what ye stand to gain.

speaker: Hating Man
line_text: Now that's a face I dislike. It's the eyes... Beady, shinin'... Eyes that see but ne'er show. You know the sort. Eh, whom do I speak of? Vayne, or course! Only a man like that could do what he's done, killin' his own two brothers in cold blood for opposin' the Emperor... / Now that's a face I dislike. It's the nose... Pointy, probin'. A nose that smells but ne'er tells. You know the sort. Eh, whom do I speak of? His name was Daguza...and he was the stinkin'est, foulest cretin I ever knew!

speaker: Fisherman
line_text: What can ye catch here? Well, lots o' things, I s'pose. Depends on what yer fishin' for. Me? I'm fishin' fer ma past...fer the fire o' ma youth. What? No, ye cannae feed a family with the past. But ye can keep yerself warm at night. / What can ye catch here? Well, I'm not sure what ye'd be able t' catch. Me? I'm hopin' t' catch ma supper!

speaker: Braggart; Defiant Lad
line_text: Me dad's the 'ead of one o' them big entry-prizes up in the City! / Ye mean 'e was the 'ead. 'E ain't the 'ead no more. There's lots o' them 'round 'ere. Them as used be 'eads, I mean.
flags_set: Bank2048 0x03F8: Once set, the name tag reads "Braggart" instead of "Archadian Vulgar"; talking to the character sets it / Bank2048 0x03F9: Once set, the name tag reads "Defiant Lad" instead of "Archadian Vulgar"; talking to the character sets it

speaker: Resting Man
line_text: D'ye wonder why I sit here, doin' naught day- come, day-go? I've done me bit for the Empire, that's why. I've earned me rest. Don't you ever fancy a rest, young 'un? / D'ye wonder why I sit here, doin' naught day- come, day-go? I've done me bit for the Empire, that's why. I've earned me rest. Don't you ever fancy a rest, young 'un?

speaker: Frank Woman
line_text: Do you have business with us? I'll tell you straight out, we've no money, so don't even bother trying to relieve us of it. / Have you got business with us? If it's love you seek, why I had plenty. But I've gone and given it all to my husband. I'm afraid you're out of luck.

speaker: Dreaming Man; Sensible Man
line_text: Brother, brother mine! If we'd only bought them cockatrices when we 'ad the chance, why, we'd be rich men today, so we would. / Brother, brother mine. Cockatrice meat's not 'alf as tasty as they'd 'ave you believe. This recent int'rest in 'em's a fad, you mark my words. Nah, cockatrices or no, our fate's the same. / This big ol' lady cockatrice came galumphin' out o' nowhere, jus' now. There was this other cockatrice here, see, and the two of 'em went off somewhere together. If I didn't know any better, I'd say it was love. / It seemed to me they was cryin'. Or maybe that was laughin'? It's hard to tell with cockatrices. / That reminds me. We plucked that cockatrice out o' Giza, didn't we. I suppose it was lonely, out here in the big city all alone. Poor thing.
flags_set: Bank2048 0x0412: Once set, the name tag reads "Dreaming Man" instead of "Archadian Vulgar"; talking to the character sets it / Bank2048 0x0413: Once set, the name tag reads "Sensible Man" instead of "Archadian Vulgar"; talking to the character sets it

speaker: Busy Girl
line_text: Wot am I doin'? Gatherin' tidbits o' knowledge, that's wot! Think I got bags o' time like you oldies? 'Cos I ain't! / Wot am I doin'? There's knowledge wot needs gatherin', an' I plan on gatherin' it! Think I got bags o' time like you oldies? 'Cos I ain't! I do 'ave a question though... Er... This knowledge...wot's it all about?

speaker: Fresh Ardent
line_text: Who am I? Ain't it plain to see? I'm one o' the many wot tried to make it up in the City 'n' fell back down 'ere. If only I 'adn't signed that paper... Yeah, I was an ardent with the rest of 'em. All it took was one broker, one bindin' agreement, and nary a scruple in sight. If I find 'im, I'll... Eh? Did ya want somethin'? Oh, 'ow to get to the City? Up these stairs, then off to the west. Entrance's up there. Better be prepared, mate. / Wot's that!? The broker wot took me in's down 'ere in Oldtown!? 'Ang on a minute! I thought that ol' geezer I passed just now looked familiar! Why, that little— Grrrrrr! / When I sleep, I sometimes dream these dreams. I'm in the City again, meetin' folk. Makin' deals. S'pose I ain't used to life down 'ere yet. / Ta for the information, mate. Turns out, the swindler was being swindled 'imself. I almost feel sorry for 'im! Huh huh! Almost.

speaker: Quiet Talker
line_text: This geezer? Nah, 'e ain't dead, not by a stretch. 'E was a soldier once. Made it pretty far, it seems. 'E's lived a full life, if ya ask me. / This geezer? Nah, 'e ain't dead, not by a stretch. Funny ya should mention it, though. Turns out, 'e was known for a particular peculiar talent... 'E was a genius at playin' dead! That's 'ow 'e made it to such a ripe old age. Soon as a battle went sour, there 'e'd be, flat on 'is back. "The Stone Warrior," they called 'im. Heh heh!

speaker: Leaving Man; Waiting Woman
line_text: I'm off tomorrow...to destiny! Mark my words: I'll be the richest man in Archades soon, and I'll bring you a diamond big enough to prove it! / So soon? Ah, no, I knew 'twould come in time. Spare me the diamond. Just...stay true. I'll be waiting.
flags_set: Bank2048 0x03FF: Once set, the name tag reads "Leaving Man" instead of "Archadian Vulgar"; talking to the character sets it / Bank2048 0x0400: Once set, the name tag reads "Waiting Woman" instead of "Archadian Vulgar"; talking to the character sets it

speaker: Perplexed Grandpa
line_text: Me granddaughter claims she's seen a great airship. 'Course, I thought it was the Alexander, that being the biggest I know of. But her description... Mayhap they've made a new, bigger airship now? / Me granddaughter claims she's seen a great airship. 'Course, I thought it was the Alexander, that being the biggest I know of. But her description... Mayhap they've made a new, bigger airship now?

speaker: Sighing Boy
line_text: Once she gets goin', she don't half go on! I only hope her grandad sets her straight. Ain't my place to worry about it, I s'pose. (sigh) / Accordin' to what she's been sayin', this airship she saw weren't wide across, but stacked up high! A bloomin' thundercloud, that's what she saw!

speaker: Shady Seeq
line_text: Oi, you there. Ya look like someone who knows a good deal when 'e sees it. So...'ows about some moogles then, eh? I've got eight of 'em. Discount if ya take the lot. It's a bargain! They're cute, they dance... / Them moogles beat me to within an inch o' me life! I'll never look at a pom-pom the same way again... / Them moogles beat me to within an inch o' me life! I'll never look at a pom-pom the same way again...

speaker: Suspicious Woman
line_text: That seeq over there seems a bit dodgy. Says he's a merchant of some sort, but I haven't seen him peddling any wares. / I knew that seeq was up to no good! He was selling moogles! Can you believe that? He led 'em right up the garden path, he did. Poor little fellas.

speaker: Proud Brother; Weary Brother
line_text: Me little brother's back! The pride an' joy of the clan's come back with tales from the City! / So 'ow was it!? Don't tell me: you made a mint, didn't ya!? Nuff for all of us, I'll bet! / Well, I, er, did set up a shop. But the competition... Let yer guard down for a moment, and the next store over'll slip a knife in yer ribs... How I've wanted to come home! / Did you 'ear that!? Me brother says 'e ain't goin' back!? 'Ow can 'e say such a thing, when the 'ole clan's 'ere eggin' 'im on!? / So, yer've changed yer mind? Yer goin' back! ...Right? / I made a few gil, but I didn't have no fun doin' it. I need time to think on things, here. The moment I go back into that hell...I'm too busy to think.
flags_set: Bank2048 0x03FD: Once set, the name tag reads "Proud Brother" instead of "Archadian Vulgar"; talking to the character sets it / Bank2048 0x03FE: Once set, the name tag reads "Weary Brother" instead of "Archadian Ardent"; talking to the character sets it

speaker: Hungry Child
line_text: I'm bloomin' 'ungry. Me mum and me gran keep tellin' me that sittin's best when yer 'ungry, but it don't seem to be workin' for me. Maybe if I 'ave a chat with me mum I'll forget about me empty belly... Or maybe not. ...I'm bloomin' 'ungry! / I'm bloomin' 'ungry. I get lots o' tasty tidbits of information down 'ere, ye know... I just wish I got some tasty tidbits o' food, as well!

speaker: Wall Child
line_text: See that bridge up there? On the far side o' that is the Imperial City of Archades. When I get a bit bigger, I'm gonna be a soldier there. / See that bridge up there? On the far side o' that is the Imperial City of Archades. When I get a bit bigger, I'm gonna be a soldier there.

speaker: Returnee
line_text: 'Tis good to be home... Those who went up to the City and ne'er came back, they either made it, or fell by the wayside, forgotten. But not me. / 'Tis good to be home... Those who went up to the City and ne'er came back, they either made it, or fell by the wayside, forgotten. But not me.

speaker: Distinguished Elder; Granddaughter
line_text: Wot? We're ain't 'ere for yer viewin' pleasure, nor are we beggin', nor are we blockin' up yer precious gutter. Not yet, at least. So get lost. / Away! Away! My grandad was a right important man up in the City, don't ye know! / Hush with ye, sweetheart. Beggin' yer pardon, sir. Pay no mind to her. She talks about things she knows little of. Aye, I've a lot in me past, but today I'm just one o' the proud wretches of Oldtown, clingin' onto the underbelly o' the Empire. Now leave us be. / Somethin' the matter, is it? Somethin' ye don't like about us, is there? / My grandad was a Judge in 'is day, just so's ye know! Best get lost 'fore 'e gets all judgmental on ye! / Hush with ye, sweetheart. Beggin' yer pardon, sir. Pay no mind to her. She talks about things she knows little of. Aye, I've a lot in me past, but today I'm just one more tired old man in Oldtown. For pity, sir, leave us be.
flags_set: Bank2048 0x0414: Once set, the name tag reads "Distinguished Elder" instead of "Archadian Vulgar"; talking to the character sets it / Bank2048 0x0415: Once set, the name tag reads "Granddaughter" instead of "Archadian Vulgar"; talking to the character sets it

speaker: Cartographers' Guild
line_text: Would you like to buy a map, kupo? / What a shame, kupo! line_text: Jules You told him just as I told you? Good boy!

speaker: Vaan
line_text: Vaan I'm not sure what any of this has to do with going up in the world.

speaker: Jules
line_text: Jules Oh? Witness the power of knowledge, m'boy. See? It begins.

speaker: Commoner
line_text: Commoner 'Ey, 'tis a fight! Beasley's gone wild! / Commoner A brawl, a brawl! The moogles are riotin'! / Commoner Fight! Fight! Fight! That bloke wot come from the City's gone berserk!

speaker: Vaan
line_text: Vaan Now's our chance! Thanks, Jules.

speaker: Balthier
line_text: Balthier Never thought you'd go for such a meager price.

speaker: Jules
line_text: Jules A pirate should know that words are worth gil uncountable. Here's some words for you: The prodigal Bunansa son's come back to the Imperial roost. See? Words of much value, these.

speaker: Balthier
line_text: Balthier Bah.

line_text: Jules Sometimes an ear with tight purse strings's the order of the day. Like when a pirate decides he fancies going up in the world.

line_text: Vaan To the City? You know a way?

speaker: Jules
line_text: Jules In Archades, knowledge is power. And power has a way of opening doors, boy. Now, a fool will buy a sack of feathers for his pillow, but a wise man... He'll buy the whole stinking cockatrice and get his fill of meat into the bargain.

trigger: requested by 監督.ジュール登場2

line_text: Jules Bright boy. You learn fast.

trigger: requested by 監督.ジュール登場3
speaker: Jules
line_text: Jules I call this meeting to order. Tell me, boy, heard any rumors in town?

trigger: requested by 監督.ジュール登場2
speaker: Jules
line_text: Jules You would do well to learn the ways of the world, boy, lest the world have its way with you.

trigger: requested by 監督.ジュール登場2

line_text: Jules You lack even that many gil? Not making life easy on yourself, are you, boy?

speaker: Vaan
line_text: Vaan I haven't heard much of anything. / Vaan Actually, I did hear about a man who picked a bag of coins out of a barrel. / Vaan Actually...I did hear about a seeq selling moogles... / Vaan Well, I heard about a man in Archades who swindled for swindling's sake.

trigger: requested by 監督.ジュール登場3
speaker: Jules
line_text: Jules I need to hear before I talk. A boy would do well to see what his ears can pick up off the streets. / Jules Bags in barrels, eh...? A boy would do well to bring that morsel to a man named Beasley near here. Tell him what you've heard. / Jules Moogle-trading? You don't say. A boy has seen the dancing moogles? Go and tell them what you've just told me. To it, boy, to it! / Jules A swindler's swindler, is it? There's a fellow in the Alley of Low Whispers, come fresh from Archades. Go and tell him what you've heard.
Smells less like a capital...
and more like a sewer. / Even empires have need of sewers. / The runoff from Archades proper pools here: those who lack papers to live in the city itself.
The mighty who have fallen, and the fallen who would be mighty. / Their eyes never leave Archades.

speaker: Vaan; Balthier
line_text: I guess it must be a lot nicer than this place. / Oh, to be sure. / Archades reeks of a different filth.

speaker: Balthier
line_text: Let's be off! / We can follow our noses to Draklor.
